text:
Sam L: Heads-up: ran into a double-charge edgecase from a toolcall that was truncated mid-stream after router fallback. Saw provisional tokens + final tool tokens both billed.
Marta R: ugh, can you paste the session/trace id?
Sam L: trace=cli-7f4a, session=ssn-42. Short timeline: client opens stream -> router A serves partial tokens -> router A loses kv cache -> request rerouted to router B which completes toolcall -> client reconnects and server emits final toolcall result. Billing ledger shows provisional tokens from first partial + confirmed tokens from completed call.
Kevin T: So we have provisional attribution on first path but we never cleared provisional after fallback?
Anna B: billing-bot POSTed provisional entries with provisional=true and session_token=ssn-42. When final confirmed event came from router B it used a different path_id, so ledger dedupe never matched.
Jamie P: Can we include a canonical session_id in the toolcall/stream ACK so billing can reconcile across routers? Right now router-local path_id is used for dedupe which breaks on handoff.
Marta R: Agree. Also need to think about streaming truncation: if client disconnects during prefix only, we shouldn't bill for toolcall body until confirmed. But some routers already bill provisionally to hit SLO.
Kevin T: Proposed change: attach session_id + provisional_marker + origin_router to provisional ledger entries. Then when final confirmed event arrives with same session_id we reconcile and either convert provisional->final or subtract provisional. That requires router code to include session_id in toolcall events.
Sam L: Example event shapes we could standardize: 
```{ event_type: "toolcall_provisional", session_id: "ssn-42", path_id: "rA-123", tokens_provisional: 120 }
{ event_type: "toolcall_confirmed", session_id: "ssn-42", path_id: "rB-456", tokens_confirmed: 350 }
```
Marta R: That would let billing do session-level dedupe independent of path_id. But careful: we need a TTL on session dedupe window (e.g., 60s) to avoid keeping state forever.
Anna B: TTL ok. But for compliance we also need an immutable audit trail. So convert provisional entries to a "pending" state instead of deleting. Then a confirmed event marks status=final and records delta.
Jamie P: UX question: console should show provisional vs confirmed cost in per-route dashboards. Right now SRE sees spikes and gets paged because provisional shows as final. We should add a provisional column and a filter.
Kevin T: Also routing policies: if fallback often triggers billing churn, maybe we route by session_affinity to reduce handoffs for tool-heavy flows. Could be a knob on Dedicated vs Hosted tiers.
Sam L: Implementation plan? I can send a tiny RFC: (1) add session_id mandatory on stream open, (2) propagate session_id with toolcall events, (3) billing ledger accepts session_id and supports provisional->confirmed reconciliation, (4) console adds provisional state.
Marta R: Also add metric: provisional_delta_rate = (provisional_tokens - confirmed_tokens)/provisional_tokens, to track mismatch.
Anna B: I can prototype ledger changes. Need schema changes: add session_id string, status enum (pending, final), origin_router.
Sam L: Thanks. @deploy-bot can we tag a canary for routing change once ledger + session propagation is in?
billing-bot: Noted. Creating ticket BI-1428 to track ledger schema + reconciliation logic.
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: eng-platform/routing-session-id-prop -> canary-1 on prod-1, ETA tomorrow 10:00 PST.
Kevin T: One more edge: toolcalls invoked by functions (tool-call chaining) may create nested session contexts. Need to ensure we propagate same session_id for nested toolcalls or aggregate under parent. Otherwise nested calls produce separate provisional entries.
Marta R: Good catch. Session inheritance rule: child calls inherit parent session_id unless client explicitly overrides. Add to RFC.
Sam L: OK sending RFC draft in ~30m. If folks can review quickly we can ship proto to canary. :+1:
